referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split-less top hero with brand/logo lockup, large centered headline, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list beneath; emphasis is text-first rather than media-led.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Long-form landing page composed of stacked content bands: hero, trust, feature blocks, integrations, and conversion form; each section separated by clear vertical spacing and occasional visual contrast shifts.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily simple informational cards/tiles with light borders or subtle elevation; content is structured in evenly sized blocks with icon-led or heading-led feature summaries.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears in the hero and conversion form; secondary/alternative CTA is presented as a nearby supporting action. CTA hierarchy is straightforward, high-contrast, and conversion-focused.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No explicit pricing module detected in the provided reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided HTML excerpt; footer pattern cannot be inferred confidently.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the hero; if present, it is brand/logo oriented rather than product demo or illustrative imagery. Content relies on text and feature lists over large media panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-led sections with section labels, headline, short description, then multi-column feature grids. The structure favors readable summaries and progressive disclosure through separate sections for core features and integrations.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture form block placed after the hero, visually isolated in its own section/card, with multiple hidden tracking fields and a strong conversion headline above the form.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static informational layout with no clear motion system exposed in the provided markup; interactions appear limited to standard form behavior.

designNotes: Use concise, high-clarity copy blocks with strong hierarchy.
Keep conversion elements visible above the fold and repeated near decision points.

personality.buyer: Enterprises and businesses seeking unified communication, collaboration, and productivity
personality.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is a collaboration and productivity suite for business teams, so it fits the HR/productivity-collaboration category best. The visual language should feel clean, workflow-driven, and enterprise-ready rather than dark or overly flashy. Since brandColors.primary is not a distinct enterprise hue beyond Zoho's orange brand identity, the page should use Zoho's orange as the core brand accent while balancing it with white, soft grey, and deep charcoal for premium contrast.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is medium-long, so 48px keeps it strong while preserving balance in a split-layout enterprise landing page.

colours.colourReason: Zoho Workplace is a productivity suite, so the page should feel clear, structured, and trustworthy. The brand's orange becomes the signature action color, paired with white and soft neutral surfaces for a polished B2B look. Dark charcoal is used sparingly for text and contrast, not as a dominant theme.

layout.heroReason: The product is a unified workspace with multiple apps, so a split hero works best to show the promise of integration while keeping the value proposition front and center.
layout.featureReason: There are four primary features, which should be presented as a premium 3-column grid with one highlighted card or split into a 3+1 rhythm for visual hierarchy.
layout.darkSectionFor: proof bar, insight/stat section, and app-integration showcase

personality.imageryDirection: Use a crisp product-led collage showing Zoho Workplace app tiles, email inbox, chat, document editor, and meeting UI layered on a clean workspace frame. Add floating chips for 'Mail', 'Cliq', 'Writer', 'Meeting', and 'Zia AI'. Keep the composition asymmetrical with subtle shadow depth, glassy panels, and a few contextual enterprise icons. If exact product screenshots are unavailable, build a polished abstract UI shell in PNG with inbox, calendar, and collaboration panels.
personality.designPersonality: Premium and efficient, like a well-run operations dashboard translated into a marketing page. Clean white space, orange-led CTAs, structured cards, and enterprise proof cues create a trustworthy productivity-first experience with a distinctly Indian SaaS brand identity.

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a strong centered hero with no media split. Keep the headline prominent, the subheadline concise, and the benefit line compact. Primary CTA should dominate visually, with secondary CTA as a lighter supporting action.
layoutStrategy.features: Stack feature sections in a long-form rhythm, each with a clear heading, short description, and card grid. Keep visual changes subtle but distinct between sections to prevent monotony.
layoutStrategy.proof: Place trust signals early, then support them with integration breadth, quantified insights, and testimonials. Use light grey or tint-backed separators to create credibility checkpoints.
layoutStrategy.pricing: Use a centered conversion card with checklist inclusions and one clear CTA. Since no price is provided, avoid pricing hierarchy that implies a missing number; focus on package value and readiness.
layoutStrategy.form: No form section is included in the input, so do not reserve layout space for lead capture forms. Keep conversion focused on CTA buttons and purchase readiness content.

designIntent.tokenProfileHint: Use default product tokens with a warmth-people bias: Plus Jakarta Sans headings, Inter body, purple primary with warm orange accent accents, white cards, light grey section separators, and subtle elevation for cards and proof blocks.
designIntent.figmaReadySummary: Design a long-form, enterprise-facing single-product landing page for Zoho Workplace. Start with a centered text-first hero, immediately followed by trust proof. Build the page as stacked card-based content bands: core features, business growth features, integrations, quantified insight cards, inclusion-led pricing, testimonials, and a final security reassurance close. Prioritize clarity, scannability, and conversion confidence over decorative visuals. Keep motion subtle, section spacing generous, and trust signals visible early.

figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: Use Techjockey default typography for collaboration/productivity products: Plus Jakarta Sans for headings and Inter for body. Apply warm-people colour logic with primary #5c4ef5 and accent #f97316. Hero should be strong colour-led with white text, secondary sections on light grey/white bands, and feature cards using the shared Techjockey card system.

sections.variantHint: Centered text-first hero, no media, brand-colour background, compact benefit list beneath CTAs
sections.notes: Use a centered hero frame with logo/brand lockup, headline, subheadline, supporting line, and two CTAs side by side with 16px gap. Add the supporting line as a compact benefit list or microcopy row: Easy Setup & Quick Onboarding; A Made in India solution; 24x7 Support; Offer: Get Your Free Trial. Because there is no UI screenshot, do not add media. Hero should use the warm-people palette with white text and solid accent primary CTA.

Render on a light grey band. Include the badge text 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally' and the customer count stat. Use a horizontal row with dividers between items. Keep it compact and immediately below the hero.

sections.frameName: Feature Grid / Why Choose Zoho Workplace?
sections.variantHint: 3-column feature cards, 4 items, white cards with borders
sections.notes: This section has 4 features so use a 2-column grid on desktop for visual balance, with consistent white cards, 1px border, 12px radius, and 24px padding. No icons are provided, so use coloured SVG icon slots from the system rather than placeholders. Include label 'FEATURES', headline, and description above the grid.

sections.variantHint: 2-column grid or modular feature cards, 4 items
sections.notes: Use the same card system as the prior feature block to maintain design consistency. Since this is another 4-feature section, keep a 2-column desktop grid with a section header and supportive copy. Ensure card titles remain short and scannable.

Use a 3-column grid with the 5 integration categories arranged as compact cards. Keep category titles prominent and descriptions concise. Avoid inventing logos; use text-first chips or simple app-category icon slots. This section should feel lighter than the core features.

Treat this as an insight-stat block rather than a generic feature grid. Use 4 equal cards with the percentage as the dominant element and the explanatory copy below. Keep the section visually distinct with a subtle tinted background and strong metric hierarchy.

sections.variantHint: Single centered pricing card with includes checklist
sections.notes: Even though pricing values are blank, create the pricing card structure from the design system so it is ready for data binding. Include the plan name, placeholders for price/original price/discount if supplied later, the includes checklist, and the CTA. If pricing is absent at runtime, preserve the card layout and emphasize the plan inclusions.

sections.variantHint: 3-column testimonial cards with star rating and left accent border
sections.notes: Render 5 testimonials in a 3-column desktop grid. Use the Techjockey testimonial card pattern with gold star rating, italic quote, bold author name, and grey designation/company. Maintain consistent card heights where possible and preserve quote length without truncation.

sections.variantHint: Centered conversion banner using extras content
sections.notes: Use the extra content to build a dedicated conversion banner: headline 'Create a Secure Digital Workspace' and supporting copy about privacy-first enterprise cloud capabilities. Keep the product name and 'Get Your Free Trial' as the CTA text. This is a lightweight branded CTA band before the final testimonial or footer close.

sections.variantHint: Text-only stacked hero with full-width stacked CTAs
sections.notes: Stack all hero elements vertically. Keep headline sizing reduced for 16+ words. CTAs must be full-width and stacked with primary first. Use the same supporting line content, but compress it into 2-4 lines or a compact bullet row for mobile readability.
Convert the horizontal trust bar into a stacked mobile trust block. Keep the trust badge and customer count visible without requiring horizontal scrolling. Preserve light grey background separation.

sections.frameName: Feature Grid / Why Choose Zoho Workplace?
sections.notes: Convert the feature grid to a single-column card stack. Preserve card spacing and border treatment. Keep the section header above the cards and maintain the same card component family as desktop.
Keep the same stacked mobile card system for consistency. Do not introduce accordions unless necessary; the content should remain readable as a continuous scroll section.
Render each integration category as a separate compact card in a vertical list. Keep labels and descriptions short; prioritize scanability over dense layout.

sections.variantHint: Stacked metric cards with bold percentage headings
sections.notes: Use a stacked mobile metrics presentation with each percentage prominently shown. Keep each stat card full-width and separated clearly for easy reading.

On mobile, make the pricing card full-width and keep the includes list readable in a vertical checklist. If the price is missing, preserve placeholders so the card remains structurally consistent. CTA must be full-width.
Convert testimonial cards into a vertical stack. Keep star rating, italic quote, and author details intact. Ensure the content remains readable without carousel dependency.
Keep the conversion banner simplified for mobile with headline, supporting copy, and one primary CTA. Use the same message as desktop, but prioritize vertical rhythm and full-width button treatment.

figmaExecutionNotes: Use a single design system for cards, buttons, badges, and section headers so desktop and mobile stay structurally consistent.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a split hero on a white canvas with Zoho orange as the dominant action accent. Keep the left side text-heavy and enterprise-focused, with a short trust row beneath the CTAs. On the right, show a layered product-led collage of inbox, chat, document, calendar, and meeting panels arranged like a polished dashboard stack with soft shadows and subtle depth. Avoid generic stock photography; prioritize UI realism and app integration cues. Use rounded orange CTAs, charcoal headings, soft grey support text, and one highlighted proof badge near the visual to reinforce credibility.

mustHaveMoments: Centered text-first hero with product value proposition, short support line, and immediate dual CTA exposure
Trust proof band showing 100,000+ businesses globally to reduce hesitation early
Feature-led sections that explain unified email, collaboration, remote access, and AI productivity in a scannable format
Integration section to reinforce ecosystem fit and enterprise usability
Pricing/inclusions block that clarifies what is bundled and removes purchase ambiguity
Testimonial strip or quote cluster to validate real-world productivity and ease-of-use outcomes
Security-focused section emphasizing SSO, MFA, spam protection, and privacy-first enterprise controls
Final conversion section with free trial reinforcement and low-friction close
avoidPatterns: Hero layouts that depend on large product imagery or media-first storytelling
Overly decorative or playful visual language that weakens enterprise credibility
Long unbroken paragraphs without scannable cards, bullets, or section breaks
Too many competing CTAs above the fold
Generic SaaS messaging that does not clearly position unified communication and collaboration
Heavy comparison framing that distracts from single-product conversion
strategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is being sold to enterprises and businesses that are already aware of the category and are evaluating a practical productivity suite. The page should therefore prioritize lead generation through a product-led, efficiency-focused narrative with strong proof early in the journey. A centered, text-first hero aligns with the supplied reference pattern and works well for a long-form single-product page where clarity matters more than spectacle. Trust should be introduced with hard numbers and global adoption because the audience is enterprise-oriented and likely risk-sensitive. The page density should be balanced to dense because the content volume is long and includes multiple feature sets, integrations, pricing inclusions, testimonials, and security messaging. Strong CTAs are appropriate because the content includes a free trial offer and a purchase-assisting conversion path. The overall design should feel efficient, secure, and enterprise-ready, with repeated moments that reduce friction and reinforce value.

referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture form block placed after the hero, visually isolated in its own section/card, with multiple hidden tracking fields and a strong conversion headline above the form.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static informational layout with no clear motion system exposed in the provided markup; interactions appear limited to standard form behavior.
componentPatterns: Bullet benefit list with check/tick icons
designNotes: Use concise, high-clarity copy blocks with strong hierarchy.
Keep conversion elements visible above the fold and repeated near decision points.
Prefer structured grids and lists over dense paragraphs.
Maintain generous vertical spacing between content bands for readability.
Optimize for enterprise credibility through utility-first presentation rather than decorative visuals.

mustHaveMoments: Centered text-first hero with product value proposition, short support line, and immediate dual CTA exposure
Trust proof band showing 100,000+ businesses globally to reduce hesitation early
Feature-led sections that explain unified email, collaboration, remote access, and AI productivity in a scannable format
Integration section to reinforce ecosystem fit and enterprise usability
Pricing/inclusions block that clarifies what is bundled and removes purchase ambiguity
Testimonial strip or quote cluster to validate real-world productivity and ease-of-use outcomes
Security-focused section emphasizing SSO, MFA, spam protection, and privacy-first enterprise controls
Final conversion section with free trial reinforcement and low-friction close
avoidPatterns: Hero layouts that depend on large product imagery or media-first storytelling
Overly decorative or playful visual language that weakens enterprise credibility
Long unbroken paragraphs without scannable cards, bullets, or section breaks
Too many competing CTAs above the fold
Generic SaaS messaging that does not clearly position unified communication and collaboration
Heavy comparison framing that distracts from single-product conversion
designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is being sold to enterprises and businesses that are already aware of the category and are evaluating a practical productivity suite. The page should therefore prioritize lead generation through a product-led, efficiency-focused narrative with strong proof early in the journey. A centered, text-first hero aligns with the supplied reference pattern and works well for a long-form single-product page where clarity matters more than spectacle. Trust should be introduced with hard numbers and global adoption because the audience is enterprise-oriented and likely risk-sensitive. The page density should be balanced to dense because the content volume is long and includes multiple feature sets, integrations, pricing inclusions, testimonials, and security messaging. Strong CTAs are appropriate because the content includes a free trial offer and a purchase-assisting conversion path. The overall design should feel efficient, secure, and enterprise-ready, with repeated moments that reduce friction and reinforce value.

issues.problem: The content layout lacks clear visual hierarchy, making it difficult for users to easily scan and find information.
issues.fix: Introduce more distinct typographic sizes and weights, and ensure distinct spacing between sections for better readability.

issues.problem: The feature sections seem monotonous and overly dense, contributing to potential reader fatigue.
issues.fix: Consider breaking up large blocks of text with imagery or icons to add visual interest and allow for better visual scanning.

issues.problem: Multiple CTAs appear early in the content without much differentiation. This could lead to confusion about the primary action.
issues.fix: Clarify the primary CTA and reduce the visual prominence of secondary actions initially.

issues.problem: The design relies too heavily on text and lacks engaging visual elements.
issues.fix: Introduce more visual elements such as icons, illustrative graphics, or infographics to break the text and maintain user interest.

issues.problem: Trust elements are not prominently placed or highlighted early in the user journey, which could deter trust-building.
issues.fix: Place trust badges or statistics more prominently at the header or top section to build credibility immediately.

designReview.repairPrompt: Improve the hierarchy with varied typographic scales and clear section breaks. Simplify the conversion pathway by emphasizing a single primary CTA early on. Enhance visual dynamism with graphical elements and iconography to maintain engagement.

strengths.highlight: The design uses a clean and professional color scheme that aligns well with enterprise expectations.

Desktop.variantHint: Centered text-first hero, no media, brand-colour background, compact benefit list beneath CTAs
Desktop.notes: Use a centered hero frame with logo/brand lockup, headline, subheadline, supporting line, and two CTAs side by side with 16px gap. Add the supporting line as a compact benefit list or microcopy row: Easy Setup & Quick Onboarding; A Made in India solution; 24x7 Support; Offer: Get Your Free Trial. Because there is no UI screenshot, do not add media. Hero should use the warm-people palette with white text and solid accent primary CTA.

Render on a light grey band. Include the badge text 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally' and the customer count stat. Use a horizontal row with dividers between items. Keep it compact and immediately below the hero.

Desktop.frameName: Feature Grid / Why Choose Zoho Workplace?
Desktop.variantHint: 3-column feature cards, 4 items, white cards with borders
Desktop.notes: This section has 4 features so use a 2-column grid on desktop for visual balance, with consistent white cards, 1px border, 12px radius, and 24px padding. No icons are provided, so use coloured SVG icon slots from the system rather than placeholders. Include label 'FEATURES', headline, and description above the grid.

Desktop.variantHint: 2-column grid or modular feature cards, 4 items
Desktop.notes: Use the same card system as the prior feature block to maintain design consistency. Since this is another 4-feature section, keep a 2-column desktop grid with a section header and supportive copy. Ensure card titles remain short and scannable.

Use a 3-column grid with the 5 integration categories arranged as compact cards. Keep category titles prominent and descriptions concise. Avoid inventing logos; use text-first chips or simple app-category icon slots. This section should feel lighter than the core features.

Treat this as an insight-stat block rather than a generic feature grid. Use 4 equal cards with the percentage as the dominant element and the explanatory copy below. Keep the section visually distinct with a subtle tinted background and strong metric hierarchy.

Desktop.variantHint: Single centered pricing card with includes checklist
Desktop.notes: Even though pricing values are blank, create the pricing card structure from the design system so it is ready for data binding. Include the plan name, placeholders for price/original price/discount if supplied later, the includes checklist, and the CTA. If pricing is absent at runtime, preserve the card layout and emphasize the plan inclusions.

Desktop.variantHint: 3-column testimonial cards with star rating and left accent border
Desktop.notes: Render 5 testimonials in a 3-column desktop grid. Use the Techjockey testimonial card pattern with gold star rating, italic quote, bold author name, and grey designation/company. Maintain consistent card heights where possible and preserve quote length without truncation.

Desktop.variantHint: Centered conversion banner using extras content
Desktop.notes: Use the extra content to build a dedicated conversion banner: headline 'Create a Secure Digital Workspace' and supporting copy about privacy-first enterprise cloud capabilities. Keep the product name and 'Get Your Free Trial' as the CTA text. This is a lightweight branded CTA band before the final testimonial or footer close.

Mobile.variantHint: Text-only stacked hero with full-width stacked CTAs
Mobile.notes: Stack all hero elements vertically. Keep headline sizing reduced for 16+ words. CTAs must be full-width and stacked with primary first. Use the same supporting line content, but compress it into 2-4 lines or a compact bullet row for mobile readability.
Convert the horizontal trust bar into a stacked mobile trust block. Keep the trust badge and customer count visible without requiring horizontal scrolling. Preserve light grey background separation.

Mobile.frameName: Feature Grid / Why Choose Zoho Workplace?
Mobile.notes: Convert the feature grid to a single-column card stack. Preserve card spacing and border treatment. Keep the section header above the cards and maintain the same card component family as desktop.
Keep the same stacked mobile card system for consistency. Do not introduce accordions unless necessary; the content should remain readable as a continuous scroll section.
Render each integration category as a separate compact card in a vertical list. Keep labels and descriptions short; prioritize scanability over dense layout.

Mobile.variantHint: Stacked metric cards with bold percentage headings
Mobile.notes: Use a stacked mobile metrics presentation with each percentage prominently shown. Keep each stat card full-width and separated clearly for easy reading.

On mobile, make the pricing card full-width and keep the includes list readable in a vertical checklist. If the price is missing, preserve placeholders so the card remains structurally consistent. CTA must be full-width.
Convert testimonial cards into a vertical stack. Keep star rating, italic quote, and author details intact. Ensure the content remains readable without carousel dependency.
Keep the conversion banner simplified for mobile with headline, supporting copy, and one primary CTA. Use the same message as desktop, but prioritize vertical rhythm and full-width button treatment.
